headlines.title: Skydance Announces Board, Adding Ynon Kreiz, Laurene Powell Jobs and Bobby Kotick as Directors and Tony Blair as Advisor
headlines.summary: Skydance Corporation (NYSE: SKYD) ("Skydance") today announced the director and advisor designees for the newly combined company, formed through Paramount's merger with Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc. (NASDAQ: WBD). The designees will join the Skydance Board of Directors, effective immediately.

headlines.title: Skydance Shares Slide After Merger With Warner Bros. Discovery
headlines.summary: Skydance shares are struggling in their first day with a new company name and ticker symbol.

headlines.title: Walmart Connect Expands Audiences, CTV Measurement
headlines.summary: The expanded services with WBD, Spotify and Yahoo DSP are intended to give Walmart's media arm a larger piece of TV ad dollars through the partnership by giving advertisers a longer reach to Walmart shoppers on linear TV networks like TBS.

headlines.title: ‘A Massive Pile of Debt’ Threatens Ellison’s New Media Empire
headlines.summary: David Ellison celebrated his new media empire with a triumphant post, but his own shareholders are already paying a steep price, and the hardest questions about debt, job cuts, and a brutal film quota have only just begun.

headlines.title: Paramount Skydance seals $110B Warner Bros deal as combined company hits NYSE
headlines.summary: Investing.com -- Paramount Skydance Corp (NASDAQ:PSKY) completed its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery Inc (NASDAQ:WBD) on Tuesday, establishing a global entertainment giant rebranded as Skydance. The combined entity moved its primary stock listing to the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol "SKYD," with shares easing around 2% in morning trading against the backdrop of broader market fluctuations.

description: Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc. operates as a media and entertainment company worldwide. It operates through three segments: Streaming, Studios, and Global Linear Networks. The Streaming segment offers streaming services, such as HBO Max and discovery+, and premium pay-TV services, including HBO and certain premium sports streaming products for mobile and connected TV devices. The Studios segment is involved in the production and release of feature films for initial exhibition in theaters, production and initial licensing of television programs to third parties and its networks/streaming services. This segment also distributes films and television programs to various third-party and internal television, streaming services, and physical and digital home entertainment markets; related consumer products and themed experience licensing; and publishes, develops, licenses, and distributes content for the interactive space in platforms, including console, handheld, mobile, and PC-based gaming for both internal and third-party game titles. The Global Linear Networks segment provides general and lifestyle entertainment networks, news networks; and hosts international media networks and global sports networks. In addition, the company offers a portfolio of content and products for television, film, streaming, interactive gaming, publishing, themed experiences, and consumer products under the Discovery Channel, HBO Max, CNN, DC Studios, TNT Sports, HBO, Food Network, TLC, TBS, Warner Bros. Motion Picture Group, Warner Bros. Television Group, Warner Bros. Games, Adult Swim, Turner Classic Movies, and other brands. Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc. was incorporated in 2008 and is headquartered in New York, New York.
